headline: Trenbolone got tested
body: Four weeks, young rats, femur and humerus measured.
punch: The bones came out shorter. Not longer.

headline: This compound shows up
body: Usually justified by mechanism. Aromatase inhibition, IGF-1 sensitivity, delayed closure. All of it reasoning forwards from receptor biology.

headline: The measurement
body: Femur and humerus in young rats after four weeks, across four groups: trenbolone, exercise, trenbolone plus exercise, and control.
punch: The endpoint people actually care about.

headline: The result
body: Trenbolone shortened femur and humerus length, though the difference did not reach statistical significance in this study.
punch: Not proof of harm. Definitely not evidence of benefit.

headline: And on bone structure
body: No significant differences in bone corpus thickness, cortex thickness or medullary diameter between any of the four groups.

headline: Which is worth saying
body: A study looked for effects on growing bone and found no benefit, with the length trend pointing the wrong way. That's different from saying we don't know.
punch: They looked. They found nothing good.

headline: The mechanism argument
body: Receptor level reasoning predicts what could happen. Measuring the bone tells you what did. When those disagree, the measurement isn't the weaker evidence.
punch: Plausible mechanisms lose to measured outcomes.

headline: The limits
body: Rat study, four weeks, underpowered for the length difference. It doesn't prove shortening in humans, and nothing in it supports the height claim either.
punch: Weak evidence against. No evidence for.
